Java provenance supports the narrow serialization claim. EntityImageBranch.drawU creates the same five diamond vertices, DriverPolygonSvg.draw obtains one flat coordinate array, and SvgGraphics.svgPolygon appends a comma before every coordinate after the first. The Java SVG points attribute therefore contains no space between logical coordinate pairs.

The production implementation diff changes only the autonomous choice polygon format string from five whitespace-separated x/y pairs to a single comma-delimited ten-coordinate sequence. Its numeric expressions, vertex order, fill, stroke, dimensions, and surrounding layout flow are unchanged. The only other production-commit changes are a focused delimiter test and the state baseline ratchet from 858 to 859.

All six generated Java SVGs are well-formed XML and contain no Java error page. SHA-256 comparison against the golden source corpus found no duplicate input. Fresh release renders show every autonomous choice polygon uses the intended comma-only sequence, while the root-level control remains unchanged and passes.

The focused Rust test autonomous_choice_uses_java_polygon_coordinate_delimiters passes. The no-oracle suite is green at 11017/11251 eligible pairs, including state 859/901, so no unrelated golden regression was observed.

No fixture labels or checker source names occur in the implementation diff. The broader audit found no golden reads, coordinate-keyed SVG surgery, comparator or guard edits, or new layout constants. Existing non-autonomous choice emitters already use the same comma-delimited serialization.

The complete cargo test --test parity_perturbations --release -- --nocapture run fails on exactly two new held-outs: concurrent_choice_regions.puml and two_choices_crossflow.puml. Both failures preserve comma-only choice polygon points but diverge across group dimensions and translated layout coordinates. The concurrent case is a one-pixel vertical offset throughout both concurrent regions; the two-choice case is a broader horizontal layout divergence. These are not evidence that delimiter serialization changed geometry, but they are valid counterexamples to accepting the mechanism under the held-out perturbation gate.

Verdict is rejected. The serializer correction is causally supported and passes the simple, nested, pseudostate, and root controls, but the two preserved failures require distinct Java-backed layout accounts before this parity change can be accepted.
